prompt:
Scene:
A top-down square photograph of the back cover of the same zine from the reference, paper stock identical, a little more creased than earlier spreads from handling. A small smear of rubber cement sits on the plywood table beside it.

Subject:
The back cover features a large hand-drawn marker illustration filling two-thirds of the page, a credits block in tiny ballpoint handwriting in the bottom corner, a torn collaged mailing label with no readable characters, and a circular rubber-stamp mark in tomato red off to the side. A scissor-cut corner trim shows a few missing paper flakes.

Important details:
Preserve exact identity established by the reference: same grey newsprint, same photocopy grain, same highlighter yellow, ballpoint blue, tomato red marker, same scissor-fray edges, same glue halo style. The rubber stamp must show uneven ink pressure. The marker illustration must be bold, black, and confident — shaky but not hesitant. Creases on the paper should look like handled, not manufactured.

Use case:
Series image 4 of 4 · the back cover closing the zine issue.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, no brand names, no clean vector illustration, no digital rubber-stamp stroke, no symmetry, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio.
